news.title: Compounding Asymmetries in Nucleic Acid Synthesis Screening: Policy Pathways for Strengthening Global Biosecurity Governance
news.summary_en: This perspective argues that narrowing global screening asymmetries requires reframing adoption as a spectrum rather than an all-or-nothing compliance threshold.

news.title: Aspire to STEM: Evaluation Report
news.summary_en: Evaluated the Aspire to STEM programme, which funded bespoke CPD and STEM enrichment in disadvantaged English secondary schools, finding it slightly increased pupil progression to STEM A levels but had no effect on science teacher retention.

news.title: Supply Chain, Energy, and AI Nexus: Evaluating AI Energy Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
news.summary_en: The authors identify the inventory of critical electrical equipment for artificial intelligence (AI) data center operations and the impact of supply chain vulnerabilities on the U.S. power grid’s ability to meet AI demand by 2030.

news.title: Can LLM Agents Select and Engage with Biological Tools? An Initial Biosecurity Assessment
news.summary_en: Large language model agents are capable of performing initial interactions with biological tools (BTs), indicating that agents could lower expertise barriers for actors seeking to use BTs. Targeted testing of agent design capabilities is warranted.

news.title: AI agents put offensive cyber within reach of novices: Comparing the performance of AI agents to humans in offensive cyber operations
news.summary_en: Agentic AI models now enable non-experts to conduct advanced offensive cyberattacks. This study finds AI agents can autonomously breach complex systems rapidly, highlighting urgent needs for evolved defence and better cyber risk assessments.

news.title: How Societies Can Succeed in the AI Era
news.summary_en: According to RAND’s Michael Mazarr, the nations that thrive in the AI era may be the ones best able to handle social shocks—and turn disruption into advantage.
